Vrf._DeStackCreates: C14, USER RULING 2026-09-07 ('bite my tongue and accept trying to space out the entities at startup'), which SUPERSEDES the R8 ruling of 2026-07-13 for 5.2. Units that share ONE coordinate - STP puts a whole COA on its assembly point - are spread onto deterministic hex rings at init, first unit kept in place. 700 m is larger than the longest shipped company formation (630 m), so no two units' formations can overlap whatever their heading. WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT ONLY IN appsettings.Demo.json (added 2026-09-20): scripts\RunC2SimScenario.ps1 sets no DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT, so a RUNNER-LAUNCHED app never loads the Demo overlay and every runner run since the ruling was made has piled its co-located units - measured on COA-STP1_Initialization.xml, 72 of 128 units sit on 10 shared coordinates. Evidence for the value: PREREG_ASSEMBLY_LAYOUT_2026-09-07 ('the spacing ruling (C14) is CONFIRMED on every prediction'). It moves units off their authored positions, so it is NOT the C# default (VrfSettings.DeStackCreates stays false, and the byte-parity golden-trace path is unaffected); a run that must reproduce authored coordinates sets Vrf__DeStackCreates=false. SCOPE (narrowed 2026-09-20, cold-start review SF2): only units created as INDEPENDENT VR-Forces objects are spread. A unit that Vrf:ComposeHierarchy attaches INTO a parent aggregate takes its place from the PARENT'S FORMATION (UG52 25.2.1), so it is never displaced and never occupies a ring slot - C14's own argument is that two SIBLING units' 630 m formations must not overlap, which says nothing about a unit and its own parent, and a coordinate a unit holds only because InitParser cascaded its superior's onto it (InitParser.cs:144-153) is not an authored co-location at all. MEASURED, not argued (--destack-selftest section 11, which parses the real files in BOTH Vrf:TypeMappingMode values): R9_Mojave_Lean_Initialization.xml 0 groups / ZERO units moved (3 platoons are taskee 114.MechCoy's own composed members and stay on its coordinate; before this rule they were composed into the company from 700 m away), R9_Mojave_Initialization.xml 0 / 0 (43 composed children held), COA-STP1_Initialization.xml 10 groups / 62 moved and STP-IRON-STORM-SYNTHETIC_Initialization.xml 2 / 12 - both UNCHANGED, because COA-STP1 declares no Superior at all and Iron Storm's two declared parents (28ID, III Corps) map to platforms, which compose nothing. So the R9 rehearsal is a no-op under de-stack and stays comparable with the D1/D1b/D3 controls, while the COA-STP1 spreading PREREG_ASSEMBLY_LAYOUT_2026-09-07 confirmed is exactly what it was. Pairs with Vrf:DropOriginVertexMeters (default 100), which stops a spread unit being marched back to the pile by its route's first vertex.
Vrf._DeStackComposedSiblings: C14 AMENDED, USER RULING 2026-09-21 (option C of the D6 harvest, scratchpad validation/v6harvest/d6_harvest_report.md PART 2). The 2026-09-20 scope rule held a composed child on its parent's coordinate on the grounds that the PARENT'S FORMATION would lay it out (UG52 25.2.1). D6 measured what that actually produces on R9 lean: the three MechPlt aggregates 24-56 m apart at EVERY sample from creation to the destination, 3 of 3 platoon footprints overlapping, 137 member pairs under 7 m against D3's 44 - the vendor's parent formation does NOT separate composed sub-aggregates, so 'held with the parent' is 'stacked on the parent' and the 2026-09-07 criterion ('no two units' default formations can overlap whatever their heading') is violated 3 pairs out of 3. So siblings that share a coordinate - including one they hold only through the InitParser superior cascade - are spread, AROUND THE PARENT, WHICH DOES NOT MOVE (it keeps the centre slot, so a taskee's route still starts where the init put it), at THEIR OWN ECHELON'S spacing: platoon 350 m, section 300, squad 150, team 100 (EchelonSpacing.cs, derived from the shipped .frm formations with their leader chains resolved - the longest platoon formation, Formation-Column-US-Army-Mech-Plt-w-IFV.frm, spans 320.9 m). NOT the 700 m company number: 700 m against a 1,097 m route is 700 > 0.5 x 1097, which is exactly what put a whole platoon permanently under the STP-837 traversal bar in run D3. Company and above are deliberately NOT in the table and keep the ruled DeStackSpacingMeters. TURN IT OFF (false) for a run that must be comparable member-for-member with D1-D6: that restores the 2026-09-20 behaviour exactly (RUNBOOK 11e).
Vrf._StartTimeAnchor: STP-850 (2026-09-28). What a task's StartTime/SimulationTime offset is measured FROM. The schema defines it as 'a time duration since the time instant of the scenario start' (SimulationTimeType, C2SIM_SMX_LOX_CWIX2024.xsd:3634-3636), and STP exports every task with offset = start slot x phase duration - the same value for same-slot tasks on different units - plus ONE same-unit STREND relation to the unit's previous task as a lower bound. Receipt (the default): the task starts at max(its predecessor's completion, order receipt + offset); receipt is stamped once per order on the task clock (Vrf:TaskClock) and the offset is scaled by Vrf:DurationScale exactly as the Duration is. PredecessorCompletion: the offset is a delay served AFTER the predecessor completes - the behaviour before STP-850, the C++ oracle's order - kept for rollback; on an STP export it grows a unit's chain quadratically (d = 60 min, ten back-to-back tasks: the last one starts at 54 h instead of 9 h), past Vrf:TaskChainBackstopSeconds, and the tail is TASKABRT'd as never dispatched. A relative (ActionTemporalRelationship) delay is a delay after the predecessor under either value. Every order in data/ whose gated tasks exist carries no SimulationTime on them, so both values dispatch those orders identically (--rulings-selftest, STP-850 section). Unknown values fall back to Receipt with an ERROR at start-up.
Vrf._DispatchReadinessTimeoutSeconds: DEFER, DO NOT ABORT (D5b, 2026-09-21). How long a task whose TASKEE IS NOT TASKABLE YET is HELD before it is abandoned, and how long an order-time materialization waits for the initialization's own creates to settle. Run 20260921T072530Z_wayb pushed the order 0.31 s after the init: the interface DROPPED T_R5_TK1 because 1.BdeHQ~PXY 'was not created' and created that unit TWO LOG LINES LATER, and REFUSED T_R5_PL1 because a live location 'could not be read'. The Way A control is the same build, init and order and differs in nothing but the order of two messages - what protects Way A is its runner's evidence gate, not a sleep. The window is as wide as the init's terrain-profile round trip: about 0.3 s when the query is answered, up to Vrf:TerrainProfileTimeoutSeconds (10 s) when it is not, and requests DID time out in that run. WALL seconds, not task clock - this bounds a wait on the federation, not on the scenario. Written here rather than left in C# because it decides whether a demo-day race is a held task or a dead one. 0 restores the pre-2026-09-21 behaviour exactly (nothing held, nothing deferred) and is the fail-first arm of `VrfC2SimApp --dispatch-readiness-selftest --disabled`. NOT covered by it: a taskee the initialization never planned (still refused at once) and a back end STP-822 has declared LOST (the hold ends on that signal, not at the bound) - a data error and a dead simulator must not become a silent 60 s wait. The operator's own instrument is the READY TO TASK line (DEMO_RUNBOOK sec 3/4).
Vrf._PlacementReclamp: PLACEMENT RE-CLAMP (2026-09-21, run 20260921T114910Z - Iron Storm cut A on MAK Earth). On a STREAMING terrain over a cold AO the init's terrain-profile query is not answered inside Vrf:TerrainProfileTimeoutSeconds, every object takes PlacementPolicy's FALLBACK arm (create altitude 0, absolute) and NOTHING places it: the create clamp needs a polygon (ifCreateVrfObject.h:210-212) and the post-create setAltitude(0, aboveGroundLevel=TRUE) needs a ground height (vrfRemoteController.h:1372-1374), and both resolve against the same page that is not loaded - which the back end reports as terrain height 0.0 (terrainDatabase.h:398-399). That run created 36 of 36 objects on the fallback and then measured two platforms at live -0.0 m against terrain of 145.4 m and 155.8 m AT DISPATCH and tasked them anyway. With this true, an object placed on the fallback is re-measured once its bound, corrected with the documented setLocation at its own live lat/lon (CORRECTION 2026-09-21: this text said 'setAltitude(0 m AGL)'; the code calls _bridge.SetLocation - VrfC2SimService.cs:3433 and :3559 - and setAltitudeRequest.h:23-25 says setAltitude 'is ignored if the vehicle is not an air-going vehicle' while setLocationRequest.h:26-32 says ground vehicles are clamped to the terrain surface; see VrfSettings.cs 'THE CORRECTION IS A setLocation, NOT A setAltitude') and CONFIRMED BY READING THE ALTITUDE BACK, and a taskee measured further than Vrf:PlacementReclampToleranceMeters from the terrain under it at dispatch is LOGGED and dispatched (CORRECTION 2026-09-25, RL-20260921-06: until then it was HELD as [BOUND-BUT-NOT-ON-THE-GROUND] rather than tasked, and refused when no read-back arrived - which ended legitimate tasks in run 20260921T143243Z; a correction with no read-back is now counted 'corrected, read-back not received', not NEVER MEASURED). THIS IS NOT A FREEZE FIX: 'born buried therefore never moves' is FALSIFIED (docs/VRF_ALTITUDE_FRAMES.md sec 5 and the sec 7 tripwire). Its justification is the placement contract (UG52 14.3.3) and the duty to report a unit the interface has itself measured off the ground. COSTS NOTHING ON A HEALTHY RUN: it arms only when a LAND object was placed on the fallback, so an init whose terrain answers ('N of N ... from the TERRAIN QUERY') adds no query, no read and no line. false = the pre-2026-09-21 behaviour exactly, and the fail-first arm of `VrfC2SimApp --placement-reclamp-selftest --disabled`.
Vrf._PlacementReclampSeconds: How long the re-clamp keeps re-asking the terrain, in WALL seconds from the fallback creates. 60 covers the ~32 s the Iron Storm terrain took to become sampleable with about 1.9x margin. IT IS ITS OWN BUDGET: it delays no create, it is not a term in the STP-852/B1 barrier inequality, and Vrf:TerrainProfileTimeoutSeconds is deliberately NOT raised by this feature - the barrier cap is 30 minus that setting (RUNBOOK 11g), so raising it to 30 would drive the cap to its 1 s floor and re-open the D5b overlap.
Vrf._PlacementReclampRetrySeconds: Minimum WALL seconds between two terrain queries for the same fallback set. The sweep runs on every 50 ms tick and a query is a back-end round trip; 5 gives about 12 attempts inside the bound without making the re-clamp a load source. One query is in flight at a time.
Vrf._PlacementReclampToleranceMeters: N - THE GAP ABOVE WHICH AN OBJECT IS MEASURED OFF THE TERRAIN (an enrolled idle object is corrected, a taskee at dispatch is logged; until 2026-09-25 this was 'the gap at which a unit is not tasked' - RL-20260921-06), in metres between its live altitude and the back end's own terrain height under the same point (both MAK-convention MSL = the WGS-84 ellipsoid, docs/VRF_ALTITUDE_FRAMES.md 'UNITS'). DERIVED, not picked: the two gaps measured in the motivating run are 145 m and 156 m, while a healthy create sits at terrain + Vrf:CreateClearanceMeters = 1.0 m. Two legitimate effects keep the honest bar above 'metres' - an AGGREGATE's published Z is a derived bounding-box quantity whose rule is NOT DOCUMENTED (VRF_ALTITUDE_FRAMES sec 1a: verify ground contact on the MEMBERS, never on the aggregate's Z), and real relief exists between a unit and its own footprint. 50 sits 2.9x below every observed burial, above any plausible published-Z artefact, and is the same number C16 already calls 'no movement worth the name'. THIS IS NOT the vertex-0 NOTE threshold: that stays at 100 m so the diagnostic line a harvest greps does not move; this is the separate, lower bar at which the interface calls an object off the terrain.
Vrf._PreflightRouteShift: USER RULING 2026-09-20: 'Route shift: ON. Use as default for any run.' Written here as well as in VrfSettings.cs because a default that changes WHERE UNITS DRIVE must not live in C# only. Set false to turn it off (or Vrf__PreflightRouteShift=false in the app's environment; scripts\StartInterface52.ps1 -RouteShift off). It never refuses a task: on a timeout, a throw, an empty tile cache or no cleared line, the AUTHORED line is dispatched. RUNBOOK sec 12.
Vrf._PlatformMoveToPerVertex: RL-20260927-01 (docs/experiments/FINDING_GROUND_MOVEMENT_PRACTICE_2026-09-27.md sec 5.2). A LONE ground PLATFORM (not a unit) whose route has two or more points is driven as one Move To per route vertex - MoveToLocation to vertex 1, the next only when that one completes - so VR-Forces plans and recovers every leg (UG52 23.1-23.2: roads, nav mesh, feature obstacles, back up and skirt, one replan). Move Along Route, which it replaces for these movers only, plans nothing between vertices (UG52 23.3). UNITS keep Move Along Route - their unit task already plans a path to each vertex for every member (UG52 30.22/30.24) - and patrols, non-ground movers and one-point routes are unchanged. STP's vertices and their order are kept, route-shift waypoints included (a vertex the pre-flight VERTEX CHECK moved off OSM water or a building is driven where it was moved to, and that move is reported - RUNBOOK sec 12a). Written here as well as in VrfSettings.cs because a default that changes WHERE UNITS DRIVE must not live in C# only. Set false (or Vrf__PlatformMoveToPerVertex=false in the app's environment) to give every ground mover CreateRoute + MoveAlongRoute as before 2026-09-27. RUNBOOK sec 11.
Vrf._VertexArrivalRadiusMeters: The vertex chain's VACUOUS-COMPLETION bar in metres (R11, docs/UNIT_MOVEMENT_RESEARCH.md :394-412). A vertex's Move To that reports success with the unit farther than this from the vertex is logged VACUOUS and the chain continues; a vacuous LAST vertex is not taken as the task's arrival - arrival evidence and the time rules decide (RL-20260921-09). 100: a genuine arrival ends inside the 15 m near-distance (or a road-shoulder offset of a few metres), and 100 m is a fifth of the 500 m arrival radius and the scale of ArrivalMinTravelMeters. 0 = no test (every completion is taken as an arrival).
Vrf._PreflightCacheDir: F3 (cold-start review of f26d4ad). WHERE THE STREAMED TERRAIN TILES LIVE. EMPTY = the shipped fallback, '<app directory>\preflight-cache' - which is INSIDE THE BUILD OUTPUT and is therefore WIPED BY A CLEAN REBUILD, so the first ground move of the next run re-fetches every tile over HTTP (60 s client timeout) against a 30 s route-shift deadline, gets no shift, and dispatches the authored line. Today's behaviour is kept as the fallback ON PURPOSE: a durable location outside the repo is not something this build creates on its own initiative. TO MAKE IT DURABLE, point this (or Vrf__PreflightCacheDir) at a directory that survives a rebuild - the interface creates it if it is missing, the file naming is byte-for-byte tools\preflight\leg_check.py's, and a warm copy of tools\preflight\preflight_cache can simply be dropped in. The resolved path and its tile count are on the start-up banner (ROUTE PRE-FLIGHT TILE CACHE), so a run can answer 'was it warm?' from its own log.
Vrf._PreflightOffline: Never fetch a tile; score only what the cache already holds. A leg whose tiles are missing gets NO VERDICT - never a quiet pass. Written down here rather than left to the C# initialiser because it decides whether a dispatch can block on the network: with the cache warm, offline=true is the demo posture (no HTTP on any dispatch path); with the cache EMPTY, offline=true makes the route shift impossible and it is SKIPPED for the whole run, loudly.
Vrf._PreflightElevationLevel: STP-802. The TMS level elevation dataset 149 is sampled at, and the FLOOR of its automatic per-tile fallback. Written here as well as in appsettings.Demo.json (added 2026-09-20): a runner-launched app loads THIS file only, and an AO-dependent value that lives in the C# initialiser alone is the asymmetry the route-shift merge's own principle forbids. 13 is the deepest level served over the MOJAVE AO and is what the 0.92 threshold was calibrated on; the Suwalki Gap is served at 12. Leaving the start at 13 with the floor at 11 lets one build serve either AO, and the interface logs which level each area resolved at.
Vrf._PreflightBuildingClearanceMeters: RL-20260927-01. The pre-dispatch VERTEX CHECK treats an authored vertex whose nearest OSM building footprint (vr-theworld mbtiles 'osm', the vendor's own building filter) is CLOSER than this as bad ground, and a nudge target must be at least this far from every footprint. 10 m = tools\preflight\leg_check.py --building-clearance, so both tools flag the same footprints; the -2 T14 stop sat 3.2 m from one. 0 turns the building half of the check off. RUNBOOK sec 12a.
Vrf._PreflightVertexNudgeMaxMeters: RL-20260927-01. How far the VERTEX CHECK may move an authored vertex that lies in OSM water or on a building: rings every 25 m out to this radius, the first KNOWN-clear point wins (cheapest path through the vertex's neighbours, so a passage point stays on its lane) and the move is REPORTED to the C2 side with from, to and why. No clear ground within it = the vertex is KEPT and reported as an STP authoring defect. 300 m = half the lateral shift's +/-600 m band; beyond it a moved vertex is no longer the place STP named. 0 = check and report, never move. This replaces hand edits like cut-A (e). RUNBOOK sec 12a.
Vrf._ArrivalApproachFraction: STP-837 AMENDED, USER RULING 2026-09-21 (option A of the D6 harvest). The traversal bar was max(0.5 x the ROUTE, ArrivalMinTravelMeters) for every member, which a member that legitimately starts closer than that to the destination can never show however completely it arrives - in run D3 twenty of 48 MechCoy members sat INSIDE the arrival radius and BELOW the bar at every sampled instant of the run, and at the moment run D6 closed the same task 42 of 57 D3 members were physically at the destination while the rule could count 23 (the whole 80 s gap). Each member is now asked for max(min(0.5 x route, THIS FRACTION x its OWN straight-line distance to the last vertex at dispatch), ArrivalMinTravelMeters) - never more than the old bar, so no task that closes today stops closing. 0.5 is chosen, not tuned: a member that starts d0 out and finishes inside the effective radius R shows at least d0 - R of displacement, and d0 - R >= 0.5 d0 exactly when d0 >= 2R, so 'actually drove there' satisfies it for every member starting two radii out - the property the route-level 0.5 had. V6g is NOT re-opened: a route whose last vertex lies inside the arrival radius of the dispatch position is refused by ClosableByArrival before any member is sampled, and that gate is untouched (--arrival-selftest replays the real V6g geometry and shows the refusal). Set to 0 to restore the pure route-length bar for a run that must reproduce a pre-2026-09-21 result.
Vrf._ModelSet: EntityLevel (default) | AggregateTacticalLevel - the model set this run simulates on (RL-20260927-01, Y-15; see _ModelSet in appsettings.Demo.json). Written here so the default is not in C# only; the runner exports Vrf__ModelSet on every 5.2 run. PRE-FLIGHT (M2, RL-20260927-01): the same key picks the rule that flags a leg in the pre-dispatch stage - EntityLevel = the slope ratio OR OSM water within +/-25 m of the line; AggregateTacticalLevel = slope OFF, OSM water (Lake areas, River lines at the vendor's 5 m MAK_WIDTH) ON the centreline stops the unit (speed-factor 0, tank-aggregated-movement.sysdef), forest/municipal land use reported as expected slow (0.25), never flagged; buildings flag no leg on either. An unrecognised value falls back to EntityLevel with a WARNING. RUNBOOK sec 12a.
Vrf._CompositionFile: C1 (RL-20260927-03; RL-20260927-04 D-2, D-8), read ONLY on Vrf:ModelSet=AggregateTacticalLevel. The authored composition a TASKED Aggregate Container is populated from when neither its STP TO subordinates nor its container template's configured members give one: rows claim fidelity-table row ids (forMapRows) and are resolved against the aggregate catalogue at start-up, every row logged (COMPOSITION ROW ...). A row naming an unknown type, a container where a unit belongs or a subordinate of a higher echelon is REFUSED - the containers keyed to it get no members and their moves are refused with TASKABRT - without stopping the run. A new row needs no code change; a schemaVersion other than 1 is refused. Relative paths resolve like TypeMapFile. RUNBOOK sec 11i.
Vrf._ContainerPopulateTimeoutSeconds: C1 (RL-20260927-03): the WALL-second bound on one container's in-place population - member creates, attach, and the container PUBLISHING its members (VrfBridge.PublishedSubordinateCount). 0 = derived: PreflightRouteShiftTimeoutSeconds + TerrainProfileTimeoutSeconds + 2 x CompositionTimeoutSeconds + 15 = 85 s at the shipped values. Past it the population is TIMED OUT and every MOVE task of that unit is refused with TASKABRT. RUNBOOK sec 11i.
Vrf._CatalogueSms: C1: empty = the installed AggregateTacticalLevel.sms under Vrf:VrfHome (else MAK_VRFDIR, which the 5.2 runner exports). A path to a DERIVED .sms - the lane-C2 authored US unit types - makes the container rule and the composition resolver read that catalogue instead; it must be the .sms the back end loads. RUNBOOK sec 11i.
Vrf._CompositionVariant: C1b (package C2, RL-20260927-04 - D-2 revised: compose to doctrine and AUTHOR the US unit types the aggregate catalogue lacks), read ONLY on Vrf:ModelSet=AggregateTacticalLevel. Which variant of Vrf:CompositionFile a tasked container is populated from: 'catalogue' (the default here and in the file's defaultVariant: catalogue units only, a PROXY where the vendor has no US type; runs on the shipped or the derived SMS) or 'authored' (FM 3-96 with the seven AUTHORED US unit types, which exist ONLY in the derived set C:\C2SIM\vrf-sms\C2SIM_AggregateTacticalLevel.sms). The resolver sees that variant's rows plus the 'all' rows. Blank = the file's defaultVariant; a name the file does not declare REFUSES TO START. THE GUARD: a variant with authored content (the name 'authored', an AUTHORED entry, or an entry naming a type of the type map's authoredRows) starts ONLY when Vrf:Scenario names a fixture whose Simulation-Model-Set-Files is the derived set AND Vrf:CatalogueSms is that same .sms - otherwise 'COMPOSITION VARIANT authored needs the derived SMS ... the fixture ... loads <sms>' and the app refuses to start. On the shipped set the authored types land EMPTY generic containers or the base abstract (docs/experiments/AGGREGATE_AUTHORED_UNITS_2026-09-27.md sec 7), so there is never a fallback. The start-up line 'COMPOSITION VARIANT <name> (...; RL-20260927-04)' names the variant, the SMS and the catalogue. RUNBOOK sec 11i.
Vrf._Scenario: C1b: the VR-Forces scenario the back end loads, for the composition-variant guard above - the runner's -Scenario value (a name resolved as <Vrf:VrfHome or MAK_VRFDIR>\userData\scenarios\<name>.scnx, the runner's own rule) or a rooted .scnx path. Its SMS is read the way the runner's Stage 0 reads it (scripts/RunnerLib.ps1 Get-ScenarioModelSet: the first .scn in the archive, its Simulation-Model-Set-Files line). The runner does NOT export it yet: pass it as scripts/RunScenario.sh --env Vrf__Scenario=<the --scenario value>. Empty = UNKNOWN: logged and harmless for the catalogue variant, a start refusal for the authored one. RUNBOOK sec 11i.
